an3.60:2.5: The Commentary divides this phrase into two: the “unexcelled” refers to nibbāna; the footing (ogādha) in the holy life refers to the path of arahantship. The analogy here is that of crossing a stream: as one approaches the far shore, one reaches a point where one can touch bottom and gain a footing; even though one is not yet on the shore, one is safe from being swept away. Throughout the Canon, however, the word ogādha—“gaining a footing,” “coming ashore”—is frequently used in connection with unbinding and the deathless. See in particular AN 7:15.
an3.60:2.7: Tathattā literally means “thus-ness.” On the thus-ness of the Tathāgata, see Iti 112.
an3.60:20.4: See also: DN 2; DN 11; SN 41:4; AN 4:35; AN 4:95—96; AN 4:99
